newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs close mostly higher, pork bellies mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs close mostly higher, pork bellies mixed.

text.p: CME hogs closed mostly higher, boosted by rising product values, while pork belly futures finished mixed.

Dealers noted USDA pork cut-out values, as of Thursday's close, were around $2.00 per cwt up from Monday and with key cuts such as hams and loins showing a steady-firmer trend at midday a further increase was anticipated Friday.
"Product should be up fairly good again today," one dealer said.
Cash hogs were mostly steady on Friday and were seen steady again on Monday.
August hogs closed 0.425 cent higher at 81.250 cents per lb with other months up 0.275 cent to off 0.150 cent.
Pork belly futures were mixed in quiet trade ahead of the release Friday afternoon of the U.S. Department of Agriculture's monthly cold storage report.
August bellies closed up 0.800 cent at 86.225 cents a lb with other months up 0.075 cent to off 1.025 cent.

The report is expected to show a drawdown in frozen pork belly stocks during June. A Reuters survey of analysts produced a range of estimates from 53.5 to 53.8 million lbs, down 1.474 to 1.774 million from a month earlier.
